mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -40.7% to -26.9%) indicates recovery momentum in consumer mobility. This trend will continue over the next four weeks, producing higher mean RETAIL_REC than the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 13.8 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the prior 28 days, or the week-on-week improvement rate reverses for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility surge (0.0% to 19.0% over four weeks) reflects restored consumer confidence and normalized essential-goods purchasing. This confidence spillover will drive discretionary RETAIL_REC spending upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 19.0 percentage points in most recent week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines by more than 5 percentage points in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 15.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -20.1% in most recent week
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to -15 or better and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -20, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL fail to move in the specified directions simultaneously in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both conditions being met.

failure_condition: PARKS recovers to -20 or better within two weeks, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -15.

RETAIL_REC will remain below -20 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:Divergence between essential and transit mobility
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to -10 or better while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 15, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -15.

mechanism_narrative: Three-way interaction among WORKPLACES recovery, GROCERY_PHARM strength, and PARKS weakness creates a constrained mobility regime where commuting and essential shopping resume but leisure activities remain suppressed. Net effect is modest RETAIL_REC improvement as commuting-adjacent retail benefits outweigh lost leisure-driven visits.
